How to find and fix reading mistakes

Reading sheet music automatically (optical music recognition) is never perfect: a sharp can be missed, a dotted note can lose its dot, or a note can end up one step too high. This page shows how to find those mistakes quickly and fix them in the app's editor.

Find mistakes by listening

Play the score while following the printed page. A wrong pitch or rhythm is much easier to hear than to see.

  • Slow down. Lower the tempo (−5 or the slider) so that you can follow every note.
  • Click a note to move the cursor there, then press Play to listen from that point. Use it to repeat a suspicious passage.
  • Compare measure by measure. The measure numbers on the score help you find the same place on the page.

If almost everything is wrong, fixing note by note takes longer than taking a better photo. See how to photograph sheet music.

Start with the measures marked “!”

Every measure must add up to the time signature: four quarter notes in 4/4, three in 3/4, and so on. When a measure the app read has too many or too few beats, it is highlighted and marked ! in the editor. This almost always means a note was missed, added, or given the wrong length. One exception: a piece that starts with a pickup (an upbeat before the first full measure) has a short first measure on purpose, and often a short last measure too, so a “!” there can be correct. Measures that add up can still have a wrong pitch, so listen to those too.

How the editor works

Switch to Edit. Each note is a box on a piano roll: the keyboard on the left shows the pitch, and time runs from left to right. For a piano score, choose the upper or lower staff at the top.

To do thisDo this
Change the pitchDrag the note up or down, or select it and press ↑ ↓ (with Shift: one octave)
Move it in timeDrag it left or right, or press ← →
Change the lengthDrag its right edge
Add a noteClick an empty spot
Delete a noteRight-click it, or select it and press Delete
Select severalDrag across an empty area, then move or delete them together
Snap toGrid: quarter, eighth, sixteenth notes, or eighth-note triplets
Add or delete measuresClick a measure number at the top, then “Add after” (with the number of measures) or “Delete”
Undo / redoThe arrow buttons, or Ctrl+Z

Switch back to Score to see the corrected staff and play it again.

Common mistakes and how to fix them

These are the kinds of mistakes music recognition programs often make, and the quickest fix for each.

MistakeTypical causeFix
A note one step too high or lowNotes on ledger lines far above or below the staff, or a note head between lines in a blurred photoDrag it up or down to the right key
A missing sharp, flat, or naturalSmall accidentals; an accidental also applies to the rest of the measureSelect the note and press ↑ or ↓ once (one semitone)
Every F (or every B, …) is wrongThe key signature was misreadFix the notes, or correct the key signature in a notation program
Wrong length; the measure is marked “!”A missed dot, flag, or beam, or a triplet read as plain eighthsDrag the right edge; use the triplet grid for triplets
A note is missing or extraNotes in a dense chord, or a mark on the paper taken for a noteClick to add, right-click to delete
Too few measures after a long restA multi-measure rest (a thick bar with a number) read as a single measureClick that measure's number and “Add after” the missing number of measures
One octave offAn 8va line, or a clef change that was missedSelect the notes and press Shift+↑ or ↓

What the editor cannot change

The editor changes notes and measures. It does not change the key signature, the time signature, clefs, bar lines, repeat signs, or text. If those are wrong, save the score as MusicXML and fix them in a notation program such as MuseScore (see what MusicXML is). Lyrics and chord symbols are not read in the first place.

Save your corrections

When you switch back to Score (or save), the corrections are kept in the browser along with the score. To keep a copy as a file, press MusicXML. When the notes are edited, the score is rebuilt from the notes, so slurs, articulations, and similar markings are not kept in the saved file.
